prompt: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to the graph of $y = \tfrac{3}{4}x - 2$?
hint: Perpendicular lines have slopes that are related in a specific way. Two things must change about the original slope.

hints.text: Perpendicular lines have slopes that are related in a specific way. Two things must change about the original slope.
Read the slope $\tfrac{3}{4}$ from the equation. Turn the fraction upside down, then change its sign.
Flipping gives $\tfrac{4}{3}$ and changing the sign gives $-\tfrac{4}{3}$, which is choice D.

learningObjective: Apply the negative-reciprocal condition for perpendicular lines.
explanation: Slopes of perpendicular lines multiply to $-1$, so each one is the negative reciprocal of the other.
The given line has slope $\tfrac{3}{4}$, so the perpendicular slope $m$ must satisfy $\tfrac{3}{4}m = -1$.
Solving gives $m = -\tfrac{4}{3}$, and the check $\tfrac{3}{4} \times \left(-\tfrac{4}{3}\right) = -1$ works. The answer is choice D.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why both wrong answers exist
steps: Choice B negated but forgot to flip; choice C flipped but forgot to negate.
The College Board builds one distractor for each half of the rule, every single time.
Say the rule as two separate actions — "flip it, then negate it" — and check that you performed both.
